newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: INTERVIEW - Benpres unit wants telecom reforms.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Benpres unit wants telecom reforms.

text.p: The Philippines' Bayan Telecommunications Holding Corp (BayanTel) urged the government on Monday to award more telecom licences and to settle interconnection disputes between various firms.
BayanTel is the telecommunications subsidiary of Benpres Holdings Corp.
"Frankly, at this point, we are feeling frustrated. We are pleading to the government to hear the public's outcry for more lines," BayanTel executive vice- president Primitivo Penaranda told Reuters.
Penaranda said that since mid-1996, BayanTel has applied to expand its service areas by installing lines in areas which have yet to be fully served by other carriers.
The National Telecommunications Commission (NTC), however, has yet to act on BayanTel's application.

The regulatory body has divided the country into 11 service areas. A cellular phone provider is required to install 400,000 lines in its service area while an international gateway facility operator has to put up 300,000 lines -- all in a span of three years or by the end of this year.

NTC records earlier showed that some of the carriers are lagging behind their telephone work programmes. Although NTC head Simeon Kintanar has announced that penalties would be imposed on non-performing carriers and rewards would be given to efficient ones, the body is yet to act on its statements.
Penaranda said of the 11 basic phone service providers, BayanTel was the only one that has installed 350,000 line as committed, which includes an additional 50,000 lines, ahead of schedule.
The BayanTel official said the government must also act on the interconnection issue.
"We will formally file a petition soon for the NTC to step in and settle the interconnection access rate issue," Penaranda said.
Interconnection and the fees for linking with dominant carrier Philippine Long Distance Telephone Co have long troubled the industry.

"Our position is that we don't have to pay PLDT anything within our service areas since our networks are charging flat rates. PLDT's position is that we have to pay them 800 pesos per trunk," said Penaranda.

The BayanTel official said the NTC should also act on the application of carriers to "re-balance" existing rates. The re-balancing will allow lower rates for international calls and higher ones for domestic long distance calls including a shift into a metering system.
At present, local telephone subscribers are charged a monthly flat rate regardless of the length of local calls.

"Without this re-balancing, international, local and domestic services will never have an equal share of the pie. If nothing is done on the local exchange tariffs, we can all kiss our investments goodbye," said Penaranda.

BayanTel invested 12 billion pesos ($456.27 million) for its local exchange activities and with the massive start-up capital requirement it promises investors profitability only by 1998. Conversion: $1=26.3 pesos
